findings.description: Gold scrollwork near the bottom of the navy back devolves into incoherent scrawl (arrow/hand-like shapes); frame linework is not mirrored corner-to-corner. A printed card back would be symmetric — this breaks manufactured-object believability at 2x.
A horizontal ornamental band is clipped at the very top edge of the frame — reads as an accidental crop of a background element rather than intentional staging.
Title band and rules panel use the same glyph vocabulary at similar weight; name-vs-rules hierarchy rests on strip width alone, and the band ornament goes soft/mushy under 2x inspection.
Hard low-poly faceted props (crystals bottom-left, faceted tree canopies) sit in stylistic tension with the fully painterly grass, frame, and sky treatment.
Faint glyph strip above the stat gems is far lower contrast than the rules-panel glyphs — inconsistent ink weight within the same specimen.
Cast card's parchment title strip carries only a rosette divider and no mark of any kind — the nameplate zone reads unresolved even granting the pseudo-text divergence.
On the occluded back card behind the set specimen, the gold moon motif partially melts into the frame line near the lower right — wobbly linework visible at 2x.

No ground plane: cards float on an abstract striped olive gradient with only a faint uniform shadow. Lighting/material integration is essentially flat, so the staging reads as a UI mockup rather than photographed physical objects.
The amber rail is asymmetric — a wide bar on the right, nearly nothing on the left — reading as a misregistered backing layer rather than an intentional frame construction.
The art window is mostly empty plum space; the small wall illustration floats low with no anchor, leaving the top half of the window dead. Weakest illustration of the set.
Monospace UI numerals (40/60) and the slashed/dotted zero on the cost badge read as debug-console type, tonally off against the Alegreya serif used everywhere else.
Radial sunburst shows visible banding between spokes; crescent accent strokes are asymmetric top-right vs bottom-left, slightly unbalancing an otherwise clean emblem.
The CAST VERSE ribbon overlaps the art window edge with an ambiguous half-in/half-out registration, and the nameplate drop shadow is heavy relative to the otherwise flat material language.

A: Frame materiality: carved bevels, edge wear, and gold/stone/foil surfaces read as genuinely manufactured premium objects across all three faces.
Ground integration: contact shadows and painterly grass occlusion seat the cards convincingly in a physical scene with a consistent light direction.
Palette harmony: amber/teal/plum families plus navy back against olive grass form a warm, cohesive, immediately premium color story.
B: Typographic craft: Alegreya nameplates, type ribbons, rules text, and italic flavor lines are cleanly set with a clear, confident hierarchy.
System coherence: identical chassis, cost badge, sigil oval, and footer grammar across all four specimens — the family reads as one designed system.
Deterministic crispness: vector-exact edges, concentric corner construction, and measurable ink-on-parchment contrast that align with the packet's metric rows.

notes: Verdict: Side A wins decisively on the weighted rubric (84.8 vs 76.0) and takes 8 of 10 crops. A delivers the warm, tactile, premium physical-card language the brief asks for — its frame craft, illustration quality, and ground/shadow integration are in a different class — but it carries AI-render defects (incoherent back scrollwork, mushy ornament at 2x, clipped top band) and evidences almost nothing for the accessibility/determinism category: pseudo-text cannot support the packet's text-contrast rows, and deltaE00 = 0.0 exact palette matches are implausible against A's noisy painterly surfaces. Side B is the packet's measurable citizen — the parchment median (204,169,132), footer contrast rows, corner-radius concentricity, and byte-identical determinism claim are all visually consistent with B's vector render — and it wins card-back and card-title outright, but its flat material language, absent ground plane, asymmetric creature rail, and weak set-card art keep it at 'clean mockup' rather than 'premium object'. No P0/P1 on either side; all metric rows claim pass and none is visibly contradicted, so no 8.9 category cap was triggered beyond scoring A's A-category on visible evidence. The ideal release candidate is A's material/lighting language carrying B's typographic and systemic discipline.
